title: Blueprint board grants full approval to three more school district plans
summary: Three more Maryland public school systems received full approval from state oversight board for their plans for implementing the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future, the state's sweeping 10-year education reform plan.
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters January 31, 2025

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters January 31, 2025

Three more Maryland public school systems received full approval from state oversight board for their plans for implementing the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future, the state’s sweeping 10-year education reform plan.

The Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB) approved plans from Anne Arundel, Prince George’s and Baltimore counties, a move that frees up 25% of Blueprint money that had been withheld by the state. They join 20 other school systems that garnered approval from the board.

Anne Arundel and Prince George’s counties had received conditional approval last month, but needed to submit signed documents to get the full clearance tjis week. Baltimore County had not been cleared last month, but all of its needed documents, including one on career counseling, had been received by board staff in time for Thurday’s meeting, said AIB Executive Director Rachel Hise.

“Unfortunately, the one that we still have hanging out there [is] my home county, Montgomery County, but I’ve been assured that in due order that they will be approved as well,” said AIB Chair Isiah “Ike” Leggett, the former Montgomery County executive.

Teachers’ union lobbies lawmakers to fully fund Blueprint, among legislative priorities

While Montgomery did receive a conditional approval last month, with Prince George’s and Anne Arundel counties, it still needed to submit “executive agreements” on its plans for career ladders for teachers — one of the Blueprint’s five “pillars,” or priorities — on hiring and retaining high-quality and diverse teachers.

Hise said Thursday that Montgomery officials must send a signed document demonstrating that agreement between the school system and the teacher’s union by Feb. 15. The next meeting of the full AIB is set for Feb. 20.

All 24 state school systems submitted their plans in March for implementing the Blueprint in their counties for the next two years. Those documents outlined challenges to implementation of the plan, and then follow-up documents filed two months later.

In other business Thursday, the board approved a contract for $766,790 with NORC at the University of Chicago, to conduct an interim evaluation on the overall Blueprint plan. The nonpartisan research organization will be asked to assess whether the current strategies are moving Maryland “at a sufficient pace to meet Blueprint goals.”

A report to the Blueprint board is due by Dec. 1, 2026. Based on those findings, the AIB will submit a report to the governor and General Assembly by Jan. 15, 2027.

According to a contract summary, the board’s report must specify if the Blueprint is helping to increase the number of teachers achieving National Board Certification, to improve behavioral health services, implement full-day prekindergarten for 3- and 4-year-old children and if students are demonstrating college and career readiness.

The board also introduced Joy Schaefer as its new government relations director. She served on the Commission on Innovation and Excellence in Education that crafted the Blueprint plan, which the legislature approved in 2019.
